title: Etale descent and Isom spaces for families of curves
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). The category $\mathcal C$ is a stack in groupoids for the fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]: isomorphisms form a sheaf and all compatible descent data for families are effective. Moreover, for any scheme $T$ and $X,Y\in\mathcal C(T)$, the sheaf $T'\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{T'}(X\times_TT',Y\times_TT')$ is an algebraic space over $T$.

proof.text: For a scheme map $T\prime\to T$ and $X\in\mathcal C(T)$, the algebraic-space pullback $X\times_TT\prime$ exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] its structure map is proper, flat and finitely presented; by [lem-sfb-space-relative-dimension-base-change] with $d=1$, applied to $X\to T$, which is locally of finite type and quasi-separated since proper morphisms are of finite type and separated, its geometric fibres have dimension at most one. Iterated pullbacks agree by the fibre-product universal property. They give cartesian lifts, and the arrows in each fibre are isomorphisms by definition. Hence $\mathcal C$ is fibred in groupoids. This also proves that every subsequent pullback remains a curve family.

Fix $X,Y\in\mathcal C(T)$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-hom-representability] with $B=T$ to $(Z,W)=(X,Y),(Y,X),(X,X),(Y,Y)$. In all four applications the source is flat, proper and finitely presented, while the target is finitely presented and separated because properness includes separatedness. Obtain algebraic spaces $M_{XY},M_{YX},M_{XX},M_{YY}$ over $T$, whose sections are exactly the corresponding morphisms after arbitrary scheme base change. No dimension hypothesis is needed for this input.

source.place: Tag 0D53, lemma-curves-diagonal, through Tag 0D1F, lemma-spaces-diagonal, and Tag 0D1C, proposition-Mor.

proof.text: Composition and identities give natural transformations $c:M_{XY}\times_TM_{YX}\to M_{XX}\times_TM_{YY}$, $(a,b)\mapsto(b\circ a,a\circ b)$, and $e:T\to M_{XX}\times_TM_{YY}$, $e=(\mathrm{id}_X,\mathrm{id}_Y)$. These are morphisms of algebraic spaces because such morphisms are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] the fibre product $I=(M_{XY}\times_TM_{YX})\times_{c,M_{XX}\times_TM_{YY},e}T$ is an algebraic space. On every $U\to T$, its elements are pairs $(a,b)$ with $ba=\mathrm{id}$ and $ab=\mathrm{id}$. Sending $(a,b)$ to $a$ is a bijection with $\operatorname{Isom}_U(X_U,Y_U)$, since an inverse is unique: $b=b(ab\prime)=(ba)b\prime=b\prime$. The bijections commute with pullback because composition and identity do. Thus $I$ represents precisely the requested Isom functor. By the fppf sheaf condition in [def-trf-algebraic-space], it also proves the isomorphism-sheaf part of descent.

source.place: Tag 0D1F, lemma-spaces-diagonal, fibre-product diagram; applied in Tag 0D53, lemma-curves-diagonal.

proof.text: Now take an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ and a descent datum of curve families $X_i\to T_i$. Each $X_i\to T_i$ is of finite type, since this is part of properness in the statement. The transition isomorphisms and their cocycle are therefore a finite-type algebraic-space descent datum. Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-fppf-effectivity] to produce an algebraic space $X\to T$ with isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\cong X_i$ that recover the given transitions. In particular this uses the finite-type effectivity assertion, whose index set may be arbitrary, rather than an effectivity assertion restricted to countable covers.

source.place: Tag 0D52, lemma-curves-stack, via Tag 0D1G, lemma-spaces-stack, and Tag 0ADV, bootstrap-lemma-descend-algebraic-space (2).

proof.text: For the descended morphism $X\to T$, every pullback to $T_i$ is isomorphic to the prescribed proper flat finitely presented morphism $X_i\to T_i$. Each of properness, flatness and finite presentation therefore holds on this fppf covering. Applying the three separate locality assertions of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] gives all three properties for $X\to T$. In particular it is locally of finite type: on etale charts a finitely presented algebra has finitely many algebra generators.

source.place: Tag 0D1G, lemma-spaces-stack, last paragraph, with Tags 041V, 041W and 0422.

proof.text: An fppf covering is jointly surjective by [def-pc-fppf-site]. Apply the covering-detection assertion of [lem-sfb-space-relative-dimension-base-change] to the morphism $X\to T$ from Step 5, which is locally of finite type and quasi-separated because it is proper (separated, so its diagonal is a closed immersion and in particular quasi-compact), and $d=1$. Every pullback is $X_i\to T_i$, so every geometric fibre of $X\to T$ has dimension at most one. Thus $X\in\mathcal C(T)$, and the isomorphisms of Step 4 make the original datum effective in $\mathcal C$. The isomorphism sheaves of Step 3 give uniqueness and descent of arrows. Together with the cartesian lifts of Step 1, these are exactly the stack-in-groupoids conditions, proving the remaining assertion.
